- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., 0.00 or -0.33) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward drag or lagged mean-reversion adjustment.
- If official event net supply is strongly bearish (e.g., net=-15.38 or -18.38) and sentiment is bearish, model underestimates downside — increase forecast low bound or add downward bias.
- When sentiment is bullish but price history shows mean-reversion (e.g., recent 3-5 days trending down), model may overfit upward trend — dampen slope or add resistance zone.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome shows early sharp decline (e.g., 3-5 days) followed by recovery, model often misses early drop — adjust forecast to reflect early volatility.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (e.g., 0.67 or 1.00) and model is trending flat, consider adding small downward bias to avoid overconfidence in stability.
- When multiple auction events occur in short window (e.g., 3+ auctions in 5 days), model tends to overestimate supply impact — reduce forecast slope or apply supply-weighted dampening.
